policy: An L/T/Y composite classification is often a spectral-binary template fit, and atmospheric variability or youth can mimic one. A composite is split only after a primary source resolves the pair or otherwise confirms it (orbit, astrometric perturbation, overluminosity). Component spectra follow the catalog composite unless a component override is listed. Candidates stay single records.

cns5-3020.evidence: Abstract: "Using Keck laser guide star adaptive optics imaging, we have found that the T9 dwarf WISE J1217+1626 and T8 dwarf WISE J1711+3500 are exceptional binaries, with unusually wide separations (≈0.8″, 8–15 AU)"; Section 3.1: "We conclude that both WISE systems are physical binaries." Section 3.3.1: component A agrees with the T9 standard, B is classified Y0.

cns5-4209.evidence: Abstract: "we have found that the T9 dwarf WISE J1217+1626 and T8 dwarf WISE J1711+3500 are exceptional binaries"; "photometric estimates suggest T9.5 for WISE J1711+3500B." The B type is a photometric estimate.

cns5-3053.evidence: Section 5.1: "2MASS 1225−2739AB is clearly resolved into two unequal-magnitude components in our HST images." Separation 0.282″ ± 0.005″. The paper's colour-based T6+T8 estimate is tentative; the catalog composite T5.5+T8 is retained.

cns5-3908.source: Burgasser et al. 2006, ApJS 166, 585 (HST NICMOS T dwarfs)
cns5-3908.evidence: Section 5.5: "With a separation of 0.″349±0.″005 ..."; "These observations therefore confirm common proper motion for this pair, which are almost certainly gravitationally bound." The paper's colour-based T6.5+T7 is not adopted; the catalog composite T6.5+T7.5 is retained.

cns5-1331.source: Burgasser et al. 2006, ApJS 166, 585; Cruz et al. 2004 (L6+T4 decomposition)
cns5-1331.evidence: Section 5.2: "The detection of a companion to 2MASS 0518-2828 appears to confirm the binary hypothesis of Cruz et al. (2004) for this source"; separation 0.″051 ± 0.″012. Component types are the Cruz et al. composite fit.

cns5-5651.evidence: Abstract: "One target, 2MASS J22551861-5713056, is resolved as a binary system, with a 4:1 flux ratio in the F110W passband. The primary has spectral type L6 ... The secondary is likely to have a spectral type between L8 and T1." The frozen SIMBAD record lists 2MASS J22551861-5713056 as an identifier of SIPS J2255-5713.

cns5-0455.evidence: Abstract: "We have discovered that the brown dwarf WISEJ014656.66+423410.0 is a close binary (0.0875±0.0021 arcsec, 0.93 AU)"; "assign component types of T9 and Y0"; "the T9 primary is unexpectedly cold".

A.reason: Composite order would make the Y dwarf the primary; the resolved primary is T9.

cns5-5403.evidence: Abstract: "Nine systems are resolved as binary"; Section 4: "2M2152+0937: This is another equal-luminosity/equal-mass ultracool binary."

cns5-1536.evidence: Abstract: "showing it is a binary with a component separation of 0.4″"; "Deconvolution of the composite spectrum results in a best fit binary solution with L9 and T1.5 components." Section 3.3: five imaging epochs; "we can confidently confirm that these sources are physically bound".

cns5-2988.evidence: Abstract: "a newly discovered 0.14″ T2.0+T7.5 binary, 2MASS J12095613−1004008AB, identified with Keck laser guide star adaptive optics." Section 3.1: "both the astrometry and photometry independently indicate that the system is a true physical binary."

cns5-3999.evidence: Abstract: "The first pair (SIMP J1619275+031350AB) has a separation of 0.691″ (15.2 AU) and components T2.5+T4.0".

cns5-1993.evidence: Abstract: "four years of radial velocity monitoring observations of the system that reveal significant and periodic variability, confirming the binary nature of the source"; Section 5: "The combined detection of astrometric and radial velocity variability unambiguously confirms SDSS J0805+4812 as a VLM binary system." Component types L4±0.7 and T5.5±1.1. Unresolved (< 170 mas). The frozen SIMBAD record lists SDSS J080531.84+481233.0 as an identifier. Model-dependent masses are not adopted.

cns5-2707.evidence: Section 3.1: "Five of our unresolved spectral binaries have been previously confirmed as true binaries"; Section 3.2.4 lists 2MASS J11061197+2754225, a T0.0±0.2 + T4.5±0.2 spectral binary (Burgasser et al. 2010) found ∼1 mag overluminous (Manjavacas et al. 2013). Unresolved (< 74 mas).

cns5-5337.reason: Strong spectral-binary candidate only (Burgasser et al. 2010, 2010ApJ...710.1142B). Its periodic variability is explained by patchy clouds; Radigan et al. 2012 (arXiv:1201.3403) rule out an interacting binary, and Bardalez Gagliuffi et al. 2015 cite it as variability mimicking binarity.

cns5-3304.reason: Spectral-binary candidate never imaged at high resolution. Gagné et al. 2018 (arXiv:1802.00493): its absolute J magnitude is fainter than field equivalents, "suggesting that the binary hypothesis is unlikely"; youth explains the peculiar spectrum.

cns5-1972.reason: Weak candidate in Burgasser et al. 2010 (arXiv:0912.3808), Section 5.2.2: binary templates give significantly worse fits than the best single template.

cns5-2271.reason: Weak candidate in Burgasser et al. 2010 (arXiv:0912.3808), Section 5.2.3; no confirmation found.

cns5-5501.reason: Weak binary candidate (arXiv:1510.08464): only two Burgasser et al. 2010 index criteria pass; no follow-up confirmation found.

cns5-3772.reason: Weak candidate in Burgasser et al. 2010 (arXiv:0912.3808), Section 5.2.7: "We therefore cannot rule out the possibility that this source is a single brown dwarf with unusual atmospheric properties."

cns5-2974.reason: Weak candidate in Burgasser et al. 2010 (arXiv:0912.3808), Section 5.2.6; no confirmation found.

cns5-3788.reason: Source of the T1+T4 decomposition not identified; absent from Burgasser et al. 2010 and Geißler et al. 2011. No confirmation found.
